title: Efficient NGS Ready gDNA from Microalga
author: Reuben B Brown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zvmf646

steps.title: Select starting material
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony from a solid‑media plate, or if the strain does not grow on solid media proceed directly to density‑gradient centrifugation.

steps.title: Prepare 100 % Percoll stock
steps.instruction: For 100 mL of 100 % 35 ppm Percoll solution, mix 90 mL Percoll with 3.5 g ASM mix dissolved in 10 mL dH₂O.

steps.title: Create density gradient
steps.instruction: Dilute the 100 % Percoll stock with 35 ppt artificial seawater (ASW) to obtain 20 %, 30 %, 40 % and 50 % Percoll solutions. Stack 1 mL of each solution in a tube from most to least dense (base = 50 %, then 40 %, 30 %, finally 20 %). Centrifuge the gradient at 10 000 × g for 10 min to solidify it.

steps.title: Load culture onto gradient
steps.instruction: Spin down 10 mL of microalgal culture, resuspend the pellet in 250 µL ASW, and carefully layer this suspension on top of the solidified gradient as the top layer.

steps.title: Pellet cells in gradient
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the loaded gradient at 250 × g for 2.5 min (settings that work for Nannochloropsis; adjust if needed).

steps.title: Recover cell disk and repeat
steps.instruction: After centrifugation a visible disk forms at the interface of two Percoll concentrations. Slowly remove the upper layers without disturbing the disk, then use a fresh tip to collect the disk and load it into a fresh gradient. Repeat the gradient‑centrifugation step 1–2 additional times.

steps.title: Enrich culture from disk
steps.instruction: Inoculate the recovered disk into 5 mL ABf2 medium, scale up to 30 mL over 3–4 days with fresh ABf2. Monitor for bacterial contamination using MB agar/broth or cytometry; alternatively plate onto F2N agar and repeat enrichment if contamination persists.

steps.title: Harvest stationary‑phase cells
steps.instruction: Spin down 10–20 mL of stationary‑phase culture at 4 500 × g, discard 90 % of the supernatant, vortex to resuspend the pellet, transfer to a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, spin at 10 000 × g, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze and lyophilize pellet
steps.instruction: Flash‑freeze the cell pellet in liquid nitrogen (LN₂) inside the microcentrifuge tube, immediately transfer the tube to a lyophilizer chamber, open the tube, and start the lyophilization cycle.

steps.title: Add stainless‑steel bearings
steps.instruction: Add 1–2 pieces of 4–5 mm 316L stainless‑steel bearings to each tube and keep the tubes immersed in LN₂ until the next step.

steps.title: Homogenize frozen samples
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from the LN₂ bath, place them in a pre‑chilled (‑80 °C) tissue‑homogenizer rack, shake at 25 Hz for 60 s, then dip the rack back into LN₂ to re‑chill. Rotate the rack and repeat the shaking step.

steps.title: Maintain cold after homogenization
steps.instruction: Return the homogenized tubes to the LN₂ bath and keep them as cold as possible to prevent endonuclease activity and DNA shearing.

steps.title: Add preheated CTAB buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of pre‑heated CTAB extraction buffer directly to each tube (still in LN₂), do not remove the bearings, and lightly shake or vortex for less than 5 seconds to dislodge the homogenate and deactivate endonucleases.

steps.title: RNase treatment at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL RNase solution to each tube, then incubate on a rotisserie in a 37 °C incubator. If a rotisserie is unavailable, place the tubes in a 37 °C heat block and invert the tubes 10 times every 5 minutes.

steps.title: Phase‑lock extraction with CIA
steps.instruction: Transfer each sample to a 2 mL tube containing a heavy‑phase‑lock gel, add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (CIA), and invert until a fine emulsion forms. Centrifuge 5 min at 10 000 × g, tip the top (organic) layer into a fresh heavy‑phase‑lock tube and repeat the extraction. Return the aqueous phase to a sterile 2 mL tube. If phase‑lock gel is unavailable, pipette the layers carefully.

steps.title: CTAB precipitation and heat incubation
steps.instruction: Add 1 volume of CTAB precipitation buffer (ensuring the final NaCl concentration is <0.5 M) to the aqueous phase and incubate in a 60 °C heat block for 15 minutes to complete precipitation of the DNA‑CTAB complex.

steps.title: Ethanol washes of CTAB complex
steps.instruction: Spin the precipitated complex at 10 000 × g for 2 min, discard the supernatant, add 1 mL 80 % ethanol, mix gently by inversion or rotisserie, and remove the liquid without disturbing the DNA complex. Repeat the ethanol wash once more.

steps.title: Resuspend in salty TE and enzymatic cleanup
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 250 µL salty TE buffer, add 10 µL RNase, and incubate at 37 °C for 30–60 min. Then add 10 µL Proteinase K and repeat the 37 °C incubation.

steps.title: NaCOOH/EtOH precipitation (jellyfish)
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 volume 2.5 M NaCOOH and 2.5 volumes ethanol to the suspension, invert three times; a “jellyfish” of DNA should appear. Spin at 10 000 × g for 5 min and carefully remove the supernatant without dislodging the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Final ethanol washes and Tris resuspension
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet twice with 500 µL 80 % ethanol, then resuspend in 10 mM Tris buffer and incubate until the DNA is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Optional enzyme and CIA cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform up to two additional rounds of enzyme treatment and CIA phase‑lock cleanup as described in step 8, if further purification is desired.

steps.title: Additional enzyme treatment, shearing, PEG/NaCl precipitation
steps.instruction: Carry out any further RNase or Proteinase K treatments now. Shear the DNA by passing it through a 29‑gauge needle ten times. Add 2 volumes of PEG/NaCl mix (from Materials) and incubate on a rotisserie for up to 1 hour.

steps.title: PEG/NaCl spin‑wash and drying
steps.instruction: Spin at 10 000 rpm for 5 min, carefully remove the supernatant, add fresh PEG/NaCl and spin again. Repeat the spin‑wash once more, then lightly dry the pellet in laminar airflow for 5 min.

steps.title: Final resuspension and quality check
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final DNA pellet in 10 mM Tris buffer, then measure concentration and purity with a Nanodrop or Qubit before proceeding to library preparation.
